stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Every electromagnetic wave — from FM radio to X-rays — travels through vacuum at the same speed $c = 3\times 10^{8}$ m/s. Sweep the three sliders: frequency $f$ (log scale), amplitude $E_0$, and polarization angle $\theta_p$. Watch how the wave shape and the spectrum-band marker respond.
stages.concept: The dispersion relation: $c = \lambda \cdot f$. Higher $f$ $\Rightarrow$ shorter $\lambda$. The amplitude $E_0$ scales the wave's height but not its wavelength. The polarization $\theta_p$ rotates the $\vec{E}$ vector in the plane transverse to propagation.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: A target wavelength $\lambda^{*}$ is marked on the spectrum band. Tune $f$ until your current wavelength aligns with the target marker. Only $f$ controls $\lambda$; $E_0$ and $\theta_p$ are free to choose.
stages.concept: Invert the dispersion relation: $\lambda^{*} = c / f^{*}\ \Rightarrow\ f^{*} = c / \lambda^{*}$. Read the target off the band, compute $f^{*}$, dial the slider.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The spectrum band and the live wave are hidden. Only the target label $\lambda^{*}$ and the empty axis remain. Compute $f^{*} = c/\lambda^{*}$ on paper, then set the frequency slider to that value and submit.
stages.concept: Blind calculation: $f^{*} = \dfrac{c}{\lambda^{*}} = \dfrac{3\times 10^{8}}{\lambda^{*}}$. Watch your units — if $\lambda^{*}$ is in nm, convert to meters first ($1\,\text{nm} = 10^{-9}\,\text{m}$).

labels.tip1: sweep each slider at least half its range
labels.tip2: compute f = c / lambda, then dial the f slider
labels.tip3: compute f = c / lambda* on paper first, then set the slider
labels.peek_tip_formula: Rearrange c = lambda * f  ->  f = c / lambda. Only f controls lambda.
labels.peek_tip_anchor: c = 3e8 m/s. Visible light (~500 nm) -> f ~ 6e14 Hz. Order-of-magnitude sanity check.

1.1: Push the frequency slider up and down — the wave stretches and shrinks. Which slider changes the wave's height?
1.2: Amplitude E_0 scales the wave vertically; polarization rotates the E vector; only f changes lambda.
1.3: The spectrum marker moves left (long lambda) as f drops and right (short lambda) as f climbs. This IS c = lambda * f.

2.1: Read the target lambda* off the band. Ask: what f gives that lambda?
2.2: f = c / lambda = 3e8 / lambda*. Estimate the order of magnitude before dialing.
2.3: Move the log-scale f slider so your marker sits under the target tick. E_0 and theta_p don't matter for the match.

3.1: The band is hidden but the formula still holds. Write c = lambda * f, solve for f.
3.2: Substitute c = 3e8 m/s and the target lambda*. Convert units first if lambda* is in nm or um.
3.3: Peek to see the rearranged formula. Then set the slider to the f you computed and submit once.
